Entertainment.title: Google Maps and Roc Nation Chart the New York Locations That Helped Build JAY-Z's Career
Entertainment.text: SummaryRoc Nation has partnered with Google Maps to launch a curated location list marking the 30th anniversary of JAY-Z's debut album Reasonable Doubt, pinning key NYC sites tied to his careerThe list spans recording studios including Jungle City, Manhattan Center Studios, D&D Studios, and The Hit Factory, alongside concert venues such as Madison Square Garden, Yankee Stadium, Webster Hall, and Radio City Music HallPersonal and cultural landmarks including Building 1 at Marcy Houses, The Tunnel nightclub, Pier 61, and the 40/40 Club round out a map that moves from JAY-Z's origins to his evolution as a mogulRoc Nation has partnered with Google Maps to release a curated location list as part of the JAY-Z 30 anniversary celebrations, pinning the New York City sites that shaped Reasonable Doubt and the three decades of career that followed it. The list covers recording studios, concert venues, nightlife landmarks, and personal touchstones across Manhattan and Brooklyn, turning the navigation platform into a geographic record of one of hip-hop's most documented careers.On the studio side, the list anchors itself in the rooms where JAY-Z built his recording legacy. Jungle City, Manhattan Center Studios, D&D Studios, and The Hit Factory are all included, a selection that spans the independent hustle of the Reasonable Doubt era through to the major-label infrastructure that followed. The Hit Factory in particular carries significant weight in New York recording history, having hosted sessions for some of the defining albums of the 1990s.The concert venues on the list trace a parallel arc of scale. Madison Square Garden and Yankee Stadium represent the largest stages Hov has occupied in New York, the latter serving as the site of his JAY-Z 30 anniversary concerts this July. Webster Hall and Radio City Music Hall fill out the range, marking earlier and more intimate moments in a live career that grew from club dates to stadium headlining.The nightlife entries offer a different kind of cultural specificity. The Tunnel, the NYC hip-hop institution launched by Pete Gatien whose Sunday night Mecca parties became a fixture of 1990s rap culture, is listed alongside Pier 61, a nearby location synonymous with that same era of nightlife. Together they place Jay squarely inside the New York scene that Reasonable Doubt both documented and helped define.The list's most personal entries are also its most grounding. Building 1 at the Marcy Houses in Brooklyn, where JAY-Z grew up, sits on the map as the starting point of the entire arc. The 40/40 Club, the sports bar and lounge he launched in 2003, marks the other end of it — the moment the recording artist became a hospitality entrepreneur. Entertainment.text: Summaryssstein's Spring/Summer 2027 collection centers on a palette of light yellow, almond green, blush pink, and powder blue, developed through fabric-specific dyeing and finishing processesKey techniques include garment-washing on an Olmetex nylon blouson, drum-dyeing on deerskin, and ring-dyeing with over-dye on a newly developed cotton-hemp soft denimStatement pieces include a mid-length Pontoglio corduroy coat with sleeve darts, a silk-rayon flannel-lined interior program, and a hand-stitched seven-fold tiessstein's Spring/Summer 2027 collection arrives as a study in process-led color. Creative director Kiichiro Asakawa has built the season's palette of light yellow, almond green, blush pink, powder blue, taupe, greige, and reddish brown not through conventional fabric selection but through a series of material-specific treatments, each chosen to arrive at a precise chromatic and tactile result.The clearest articulation of that approach sits in the season's nylon blouson, developed exclusively for ssstein by Olmetex. After construction, the garment was subjected to a garment-wash process, which simultaneously softened the tone to a time-worn register and produced an airy hand feel. A functional consequence of that wash is the puckering effect it generated between the parallel stitches of the garment, a textural detail that reads as both incidental and deliberate.Deerskin receives a different treatment. Rather than pigment-dyeing, which sits on the surface of the leather, Asakawa specified drum-dyeing for the season's deerskin pieces. The result is a deep, uniform tone achieved through full material penetration, accompanied by a suppleness that pigment application would have compromised. The distinction between the two methods is not merely technical; it reflects a consistent preference throughout the collection for processes that alter the material from within rather than coating it from without.The season's newly developed soft denim, composed of cotton and hemp, represents the most layered instance of that philosophy. Ring-dyed yarns were selected for the relief-like interplay of light and shadow they produce at the surface, a quality inherent to the yarn construction rather than applied after the fact. An over-dye was then added to bring the overall tone toward the muted end of the season's palette, layering two distinct color logics into a single cloth.The only pattern of the season is a grey-toned check, present in one version woven by British mill Moon in a wool-linen composition. The check functions as a vehicle for color gradation rather than graphic contrast, consistent with Asakawa's broader chromatic framework. Elsewhere, the Pontoglio corduroy mid-length coat arrives washed and tumble-dried post-construction to emphasize the wale, with a boxy silhouette given structure through darts positioned at the top of the sleeves. Several garments across the collection are lined with silk-rayon flannel, an interior specification that operates independently of the outward construction logic but signals the same level of material consideration.Lightness enters through the season's washable silk, worked into a shacket and a matching authentic shirt for layering, and through an extremely soft linen used across a skipper shirt and easy pants. The pants themselves are a hybrid construction: single pleats, an elastic and drawstring waist, and a fly front are combined within a single style. Women's pants take a more contemporary direction, with an extra-wide full-length style featuring side slits alongside a running short in super-light wool finished with leather piping. The season's statement accessory is a hand-stitched seven-fold tie, available paired with shirts in super-light wool sourced from either Canonico or Delfino.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: adidas Originals and BAPE Launch Exclusive Teamgeist Capsule for FIFA World Cup 2026
Entertainment.text: Summaryadidas Originals and A Bathing Ape (BAPE) have launched a limited-edition soccer capsule ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026The collection centers on "Home" and "Away" kits built on adidas' iconic Teamgeist jersey templateEach jersey is paired with a matching, heavily customized iteration of the adidas EVO SL running silhouetteadidas Originals and BAPE have officially reunited to launch a specialized lifestyle capsule celebrating the upcoming FIFA World Cup 2026. Designed to seamlessly transition soccer culture from the stadium to the streets, the collection pairs the heritage design language of adidas performance apparel with BAPE’s signature streetwear iconography, delivering a dual-set release aimed at global football fans.At the foundation of the capsule is the historic adidas Teamgeist jersey template, celebrated for its distinctive curved panels and mid-2000s soccer aesthetic. The BAPE "Home" Set pays direct homage to the World Cup's host nations, anchoring itself in a vibrant green, red, and blue Trefoil ABC CAMO. The jersey is packed with co-branded motifs, including an A Bathing Ape crest, three prominent BAPE STA logos across the front, the label’s founding year ’93’ on the reverse, and a unique "2W0G2M6" code printed along the lower back hem.To complete the kit, the Home jersey is paired with a pioneering adidas EVO SL running sneaker in a custom mismatched blue and green colorway. The footwear displays BAPE STA branding on the lateral and medial sides, alongside "A BATHING APE" spelled out in alternating English and Japanese text across each foot. This entire Home set is being distributed as a strict regional exclusive, available only within North America and Latin America.Conversely, the BAPE "Away" Set is engineered to celebrate the broader, overarching spirit of global fandom. While retaining the exact same structural details, branding points, and Teamgeist paneling as the Home kit, the Away jersey pivots to a clean gray, gold, and pink Trefoil ABC CAMO palette. Its footwear counterpart features a heavily mismatched white, light blue, pink, and gold EVO SL colorway. Catering to the rest of the world, the Away capsule is available internationally across global markets, explicitly excluding the North and Latin American territories.The entire adidas Originals x BAPE FIFA World Cup 2026 capsule officially launched on June 27, 2026. Entertainment.title: TAG Heuer Reunites With Gulf for a Special Formula 1 Automatic Chronograph
Entertainment.text: SummaryTAG Heuer debuts a 44mm titanium Formula 1 Automatic Chronograph in collaboration with Gulf.The racing dial features iconic blue and orange stripes alongside a carbon bezel.Limited to 1,000 pieces, it retails for $6,300 USD.TAG Heuer has unveiled the Formula 1 Automatic Chronograph x Gulf, the fourth collaboration between the Swiss watchmaker and Gulf Oil, continuing a partnership deeply rooted in motorsport culture. This high-intensity timepiece pays homage to a rich legacy anchored in endurance racing, where Gulf's signature blue and orange livery became inseparable from the historic circuits of Le Mans and the cinematic legacy of Steve McQueen. Designed to translate the visual force and mechanical demands of motorsport to the wrist, the new chronograph embodies both brands' shared commitment to absolute clarity and precision under extreme pressure.The watch features a robust 44mm case constructed from sandblasted Grade 2 titanium, providing a lightweight yet highly durable frame for everyday wear and track performance. Its striking black opalin dial is bisected by the iconic Gulf blue and orange vertical stripes, which are framed by a blue lacquered track and a forged carbon fixed tachymeter bezel bearing the Gulf marking. Powered by the Caliber 16 automatic movement, the instrument-driven layout includes three specialized subdials: a 30-minute counter at 12 o'clock, a 12-hour counter at 6 o'clock and a permanent second indicator at 9 o'clock. Rounding out its athletic build are skeletonized hour and minute hands, black DLC-finished pushers, a 200-meter water resistance rating, and a matching three-row Grade 2 titanium bracelet.Adding to its collectible appeal, the timepiece features a titanium screw-down caseback specially engraved with the Gulf logo, cementing its motorsport identity. Entertainment.title: Y-3 SS27 Re-Codes Blokecore With Poetic Brutalism
Entertainment.text: SummaryY‑3 transformed Paris’s Palais Brongniart into a brutalist football stadium for its SS27 runway presentation.Key looks included stripe motifs, tailored denim, layered dresses and reimagined Stan Smith sneakers.Standouts featured the Takahiro Miyashita partnership with bold graphics and Yakutat Boot TM.Y-3 presented its Spring/Summer 2027 runway collection at the historic Palais Brongniart in Paris, centering its core message on a poetic deconstruction of football culture. The show captured the collective pulse of the global game by transforming the venue into a brutalist evocation of a football stadium. Guests were seated on stadium-style bleachers under intense stadium lights and abstract ambient illuminations modeled after pitch-level LED screens. The runway itself was composed of a stark black astroturf, providing a dramatic floor for a three-part performance by movement artists whose choreography mirrored the emotional ebbs and flows of a typical football match.The lineup gracefully navigated the tipping point where athletic utility meets avant-garde sartorial expression. Mainline styles relied heavily on a staple three-stripe motif that seamlessly connected classic adidas iconography with a rebellious, counter-cultural edge. The garments balanced structure and fluidity, showcasing expertly tailored denim alongside elegantly constructed women's dresses defined by expressive layering and draped silhouettes. The runway looks established a dark, moody aesthetic dominated by deep blacks, monochromatic tracking layers and sleek athletic caps branded with the iconic white stripes.Footwear served as a key anchor for the seasonal collection, highlighted by radical reinterpretations of timeless adidas silhouettes. Most notably, the classic tennis sneaker was subverted via the new Y-3 STAN SMITH SQ, which introduced a highly formal, unexpected silhouette featuring a square toe and an elevated heel. This formal adaptation was complemented by the sleeker, low-profile Y-3 STAN SMITH LO PRO. Additionally, the brand also revived the Y-3 YAKUTAT, an archival silhouette originally introduced in SS08, re-engineering it with a highly breathable, summer-ready construction.Another noteworthy highlight of the presentation sees an array of collaborative pieces that were developed alongside Takahiro Miyashita and his revived label, Number (N)ine. Driven by a shared commitment to pushing aesthetic boundaries, the technical capsule reimagined quintessential Y-3 silhouettes with subverted football jerseys featuring taped seams, knit sweaters integrated with reflective yarns and distinct metal trims. Entertainment.title: The Travis Scott x Nike Phantom 6 Low "Cactus Jack" Pack Has Officially Landed
Entertainment.text: Name: Travis Scott Nike Phantom 6 Low Indoor, Travis Scott Nike Phantom 6 Elite FGColorway: Multi-Color/Metallic GoldSKU: IQ8140-900, IV2037-900MSRP: $200 USD, $320 USDRelease Date: Available nowWhere to Buy: Travis ScottTravis Scott has released the Travis Scott x Nike Phantom 6 Low "Cactus Jack" pack, a two-piece football collection comprising a performance cleat and a reworked indoor trainer. Both silhouettes share a consistent design language built on neon green uppers, glossy Reverse Swooshes, and an earthy brown palette across the collars and sole units, with Cactus Jack branding woven throughout.The pack's visual identity is immediately legible as a Cactus Jack project. The neon green uppers sit in deliberate contrast with the brown collar and sole unit treatment, a color pairing that mirrors the earthy tones La Flame has deployed consistently across his Nike footwear collaborations. Glossy Reverse Swooshes run on both pairs, flipping one of the most recognizable elements of the Travis Scott x Nike formula onto a football silhouette for the first time. Yellow laces add a further layer of contrast, pulling the palette toward something more maximalist than either a standard Phantom 6 or a typical Cactus Jack release would suggest on its own.The detailing carries through to the smaller elements. Cactus Jack insoles and crooked smiley heel graphics are present across both versions, the latter a recurring motif in Scott's Nike work that reads as a signature as much as a graphic. Each pair ships with a special drawstring bag, extending the branded packaging logic that has become standard across major Cactus Jack drops.The two silhouettes diverge at the construction level. The Elite FG cleat is a traditional performance build designed for firm ground, while the Indoor version takes a lower-profile shape that the source describes as drawing from the aesthetic of Nike's classic Total 90 era. That reference point is worth noting: the Total 90 was one of the defining football shoes of the late 1990s and early 2000s, and its influence on the Indoor version gives the pack a heritage dimension alongside its contemporary Cactus Jack identity.Contextually, the pack lands within Nike's World Cup collaborator program, a campaign that has also drawn in Patta, Jacquemus, Jordan Brand, and the Virgil Abloh Archives under the "Rip the Script" banner. La Flame’s entry into that lineup through a football-specific silhouette rather than a lifestyle shoe marks a deliberate step into on-pitch territory, one that keeps the Cactus Jack aesthetic intact while operating inside a performance framework.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: BAPE's Mary Jane STA Fuses STA Streetwear with a Feminine Low-Top Silhouette
Entertainment.text: Name: BAPE MARY JANE STAColorway: Silver, PinkSKU: 1M30-291-324MSRP: $325 USDRelease Date: Available nowWhere to Buy: BAPEBAPE has introduced the Mary Jane STA, a women's low-top sneaker that recasts the brand's long-running STA silhouette in one of its most formal variations to date. Available in silver, the shoe retains the STA logo detailing that has defined BAPE's footwear identity across decades, while the Mary Jane construction and mesh panel bodice introduce a clear shift in register toward a more dressed-up aesthetic.The BAPE STA's design history is one of streetwear's most recognizable arcs. Since its debut in the early 2000s, the STA silhouette has been reworked across an extensive range of sub-variants, collaborations, and gender-specific editions, making it one of the most iterated footwear frameworks in the brand's catalog. That breadth of iteration is precisely what makes the Mary Jane STA a notable entry: rather than pushing the silhouette further into athletic or skate-adjacent territory, BAPE has pivoted toward a format with a distinctly dressier inheritance.The Mary Jane silhouette is historically associated with formal wear and elevated casual dressing, a context that sits at some distance from the courts and streets the STA usually references. Applying the STA's logo architecture to that construction produces something genuinely hybrid: a shoe that carries the brand's streetwear credentials on its upper while orienting its overall form toward a more polished wearing occasion. The mesh panel bodice reinforces that tension, lending the shoe a structural lightness that reads as intentional rather than incidental.The silver colorway completes the picture. Rather than anchoring the Mary Jane STA in BAPE's more familiar bold graphics palette, silver amplifies the formal quality of the Mary Jane cut, aligning the shoe's finish with its silhouette's upscale implications.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Front office executives in the Bay Area want to unite LeBron James and Anthony Davis with Stephen Curry and Draymond Green. This aggressive push comes as the franchise tries to maximize Curry's closing championship window. That blueprint aims to recreate the undeniable chemistry seen during Team USA's 2024 gold medal run where James praised his effortless fit alongside the legendary point guard.Landing both stars requires a complex series of moves. Reports from Yahoo Sports indicate Golden State would look to sign James as an unrestricted free agent while orchestrating a massive trade for the Washington big man. Trading for him would instantly reset that clock and complicate his long-term financial security under the current collective bargaining agreement.Competition from rival franchises adds another layer of difficulty to the pursuit. The Portland Trail Blazers reportedly view the big man as a premium backup target after missing out on Giannis Antetokounmpo. Portland possesses an attractive collection of tradable salaries and future draft capital that could easily trump Golden State's offer of Butler and distant picks. Management is also heavily monitoring Jaylen Brown as they look to make a significant splash in the Western Conference.This frantic search for elite talent highlights a recurring theme for Golden State over the past few years. Climate & Environment.text: In today’s newsletter: Last week’s extreme weather should galvanise the political response to global heating. But the sad paradox is that it could bolster support for climate-sceptical partiesGood morning. You could be forgiven for thinking that last week’s heatwave in Europe would be a galvanising moment for action on the climate crisis. At one point, more than 150 million Europeans sweltered in temperatures above 35C (95F) – with several parts of the continent soaring past 40C. A heatwave of this magnitude has never been recorded this early in the year.When scientists finish their calculations, the death toll will probably number in the thousands. Spain, one of the few countries that produces real-time statistics on excess deaths linked to heat, has recorded more than 100 per day since Wednesday. French authorities said that at least 1,000 additional deaths had been recorded between 24 and 27 June, a figure that is likely to rise. They include four toddlers who died in incidents linked to the heat.
